manifesto.title: CJP Manifesto
manifesto.subtitle: Five demands. Zero sponsors. One large, stubborn swarm.
manifesto.partyDesc: A political front of the youth, by the youth, for the youth: Secular, Socialist, Democratic, and Lazy. Reclaiming the cockroach as a badge of resilience.

1.title: NEET Cancellation & Reform
1.desc: Nullify NEET-UG 2024 results. Constitute a judicial commission to overhaul the exam system. Re-test under Supreme Court supervision.

2.title: Anti-Paper-Leak Law
2.desc: Enact a stringent law making exam paper leaks a cognizable, non-bailable offence with 10-year minimum sentence. Create a centralised secure digital exam infrastructure.

3.title: Education Minister's Resignation
3.desc: Demand the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan for systemic failure in protecting the integrity of national examinations.

4.title: Free Legal Aid for Protesters
4.desc: Establish government-funded free legal aid desks at every district court for students facing politically motivated cases. No student should hire a lawyer to demand their right to education.

5.title: Digital Rights Charter
5.desc: Enact a Digital Rights Charter prohibiting internet shutdowns during examinations and protests. Ensure net neutrality, data privacy, and the right to peaceful digital assembly.

manifesto.joinDesc: Membership is open to the unemployed, the lazy, the chronically online, and anyone who has ever been told they amount to nothing. We are many. They are few.
manifesto.seoDesc: Cockroach Janta Party's five demands: NEET cancellation, anti-paper-leak law, education minister resignation, free legal aid, digital rights charter.

about.title: About CockroachHub
about.partyDesc1: The Cockroach Janta Party is a satirical political party and student protest movement founded on May 16, 2026 by Abhijeet Dipke. What started as an internet meme grew into a nationwide youth movement leading the NEET paper leak protests at Jantar Mantar, Delhi.
about.partyDesc2: The party describes itself as 'a political front of the youth, by the youth, for the youth: Secular, Socialist, Democratic, and Lazy' — reclaiming the 'cockroach' label as a badge of resilience.
about.appDesc: CockroachHub is a protest resource hub designed specifically for student protesters in India. It provides verified emergency contacts, live field updates, legal rights information (BNSS-corrected), first aid guides, and mental health support — all cached on your device.

privacy.title: Privacy & Surveillance Guide
privacy.subtitle: How to protect your phone and data during protests

phoneSecurity.title: Phone Security Before You Go
items: Enable a strong PIN/password — not pattern lock
Disable biometric unlock (police can force your finger/face)
Turn off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth when not in use to avoid IMSI catchers
Enable auto-lock with shortest timeout (30 seconds)
Remove sensitive apps from your home screen

digitalPrivacy.title: Digital Privacy During Protests
items: Use VPN at all times — prefer WireGuard or OpenVPN
Turn on airplane mode near protest sites to avoid tower tracking
Use encrypted messaging (Signal, Briar, BitChat — NOT SMS)
Disable location history in Google Maps settings
Avoid posting real-time location on social media

ifSeized.title: If Your Phone Is Seized
items: You have the right to remain silent — do not give passwords
Police cannot compel you to unlock your phone (Article 20(3))
Enable auto-erase or remote wipe if you have time
Log out of all accounts remotely if possible
Contact a lawyer immediately — do not sign anything

surveillance.title: Avoiding Surveillance
items: Assume all communications can be monitored during protests
Use burner SIMs if possible for protest coordination
Remove your phone battery if you suspect active tracking
Cover cameras with tape when not in use
Watch for stalkerware — check installed apps regularly

privacy.seoDesc: Protect your phone and data during protests. Phone security, digital privacy, what to do if your phone is seized, avoiding surveillance.

evidence.title: Evidence Preservation Guide
evidence.subtitle: How to document and preserve evidence of police violence or human rights violations

capture.title: Capturing Evidence Safely
items: Record video horizontally when possible — captures more context
Start each video with: date, time, location (say it aloud)
Capture identifying details: badge numbers, vehicle plates, unit markers
Keep recording even during escalation — continuous footage is stronger
Stay at safe distance — your safety comes first

preserve.title: Preserving Digital Evidence
items: Upload footage to cloud immediately after leaving the site
Use multiple platforms: Google Drive, Dropbox, Proton Drive
Share copies with a trusted contact not at the protest
Do not edit or trim raw footage — unaltered files hold more weight
Keep metadata intact (date, time, location stamps)

legal.title: Legal Use of Evidence
items: File an FIR with the nearest police station within 24 hours
Submit footage on a USB drive — keep the original on your device
Get a free legal aid lawyer via NALSA (15100) before submitting anything
Document your own statement: what you saw, when, where, who
Collect witness names and contact information

medical.title: Medical Evidence After Violence
items: Get a medical examination within 24 hours at a government hospital
Request a copy of the medical report (MLC — Medico-Legal Certificate)
Photograph injuries with a ruler or object for scale
Keep all prescription receipts and pharmacy bills
Do not shower before the medical exam if you were pepper-sprayed or tear-gassed
